Nagoji and Varma: new sheets and the two recurring fixes

For approval, 2026-10-08. Nothing below has been applied to the bible, the prompts or the pipeline yet.

1. Why the two men get mixed up

Three rounds of independent checks agree: under the hair and ornaments, the two approved V13 faces are one template (oval face, high cheekbones, straight nose, clean chin, curled moustache). The old sheets made it worse. Nagoji's sheet shows a hanging drop earring, and Varma's only bare-headed figure is the grey-haired dedication look, which is where the grey temples and back-of-head knot keep coming from. What reliably keeps them apart is a set of markers, and the bible's Varma line currently locks none of them, so panel prompts never carry them.

4. How the sheets get used

  • Every panel still to be generated or regenerated (chapters 13 to 28, plus the open fixes in chapters 7 and 8) attaches the right sheet for its chapter and page, and its prompt carries the markers above.
  • An identity audit re-checks every accepted panel that shows Varma or Nagoji, chapters 5 to 28, against the new sheets: Varma drawn with grey, a crown knot, the heavy moustache or no namam; Nagoji with a hanging earring. Failures are redrawn under the two-attempt rule.
  • The held regenerations (rejects in chapters 15, 17, 22, 23, 24 and 28) run after the switch, so they use the new sheets.

5. Speech tails (the other recurring fault)

Today every tail runs 60 percent of the way to the speaker's mouth and is capped at 28 pt. In chapters 5 to 12, 157 of 592 tails hit the cap, and 151 stop more than 20 pt short of the speaker. Those are the "tail points at the wrong person" findings. The fix stops each tail just outside the speaker's own head, using the face circle the selector already marks (and at most 12 pt from the mouth when no face is known). Off-panel speakers are unchanged. Checked against 476 in-panel tails, a tail run that far crosses another person's face only once.

Files: pipeline/run_chapter.py (write the speaker's head circle into each speech balloon), pipeline/compositor.py (the tail planner uses it), tests written first in test_compositor.py and test_run_chapter.py, full suite run. Chapters 1 to 12 then need a lettering-only rebuild (same art and layout, new revision numbers, old PDFs kept); chapters 13 to 28 get it automatically.

Needed from you: an OK on (1) adopting the three sheets, (2) the bible wording in section 3, and (3) the tail fix with the lettering-only rebuild of chapters 1 to 12. Any of them can be approved alone.
